items.prompt:
Which action shows a student following discussion rules?
A) Calling out answers without raising a hand
B) Raising a hand and waiting to be called on
C) Talking to a friend while someone else speaks
items.answer: B) Raising a hand and waiting to be called on

steps: Raising a hand and waiting is the respectful way to gain the floor in a discussion.

items.prompt:
What should you do when a classmate is speaking?
A) Talk over them
B) Look out the window
C) Listen carefully

steps: One of the key discussion rules is to listen to others with care when they are speaking.

items.prompt:
A student says: 'I like apples.' Which response BUILDS on what she said?
A) 'I like apples too, and my favorite kind is Honeycrisp!'
B) 'Can we talk about recess?'
C) 'That's not interesting.'
items.answer: A) 'I like apples too, and my favorite kind is Honeycrisp!'

steps: Building on a classmate's comment means connecting your idea to what they said and adding new information.

items.prompt:
Two students start talking at the same time in a discussion. What rule are they breaking?
A) Always be on topic
B) Speak one at a time
C) Only the teacher speaks
items.answer: B) Speak one at a time

steps: The rule 'speak one at a time' means waiting until the other person finishes before you begin.

items.prompt:
A student does not understand what her classmate said. What should she do?
A) Pretend she understood
B) Ask the classmate to explain more
C) Change the subject
items.answer: B) Ask the classmate to explain more

steps: Asking for clarification — 'Can you tell us more?' — is a key discussion skill.

items.prompt:
Which sentence is a good way to agree with a classmate AND add new information?
A) 'You're wrong.'
B) 'I agree! And I also know that butterflies migrate in winter.'
C) 'I already said that.'
items.answer: B) 'I agree! And I also know that butterflies migrate in winter.'

steps: Starting with agreement and then adding new connected information is the correct way to build on a classmate's comment.

items.prompt:
What does 'gaining the floor' mean in a discussion?
A) Picking up something off the floor
B) Getting your turn to speak in a respectful way
C) Standing on the floor during class
items.answer: B) Getting your turn to speak in a respectful way

steps: 'Gaining the floor' is an expression meaning it is your turn to speak. You do this respectfully by waiting or raising your hand.

items.prompt:
A student says the same thing over and over during a discussion and does not connect to what others said. Is this good discussion behavior?
A) Yes — it shows she is confident
B) No — good discussions involve listening and adding new ideas, not repeating yourself
C) Yes — repeating yourself helps people remember
items.answer: B) No — good discussions involve listening and adding new ideas, not repeating yourself

steps: Good discussion contributors listen and then add new or connected information, not repeat the same point.

items.prompt:
A student starts talking about a completely different topic in the middle of a discussion about ocean animals. Is this following the discussion rules?
A) Yes — any topic is fine
B) No — discussion should stay on the topic that is being discussed
C) Yes — changing topics makes discussions interesting
items.answer: B) No — discussion should stay on the topic that is being discussed

steps: Discussion rules include speaking about the topics and texts under discussion. Changing topics abruptly does not follow the rules.

items.prompt:
A student wants to share an idea but two classmates are still talking. What should she do?
A) Wait until they are done, then raise her hand
B) Shout her idea louder than them
C) Give up and say nothing
items.answer: A) Wait until they are done, then raise her hand

steps: Waiting and then raising your hand is the respectful way to gain the floor.

items.prompt:
Which sentence shows a student LINKING their comment to what a classmate said?
A) 'I don't have anything to say.'
B) 'That reminds me of what Jaylen said — whales also travel in groups.'
C) 'I wasn't listening.'
items.answer: B) 'That reminds me of what Jaylen said — whales also travel in groups.'

steps: Linking your comment to a classmate's remark ('That reminds me of what Jaylen said') is how you build on others' talk.

items.prompt:
Why is listening to others important in a discussion?
A) So you know when to raise your hand only
B) So you can understand their ideas and respond in a way that builds on them
C) So you can tell if they are right or wrong
items.answer: B) So you can understand their ideas and respond in a way that builds on them

steps: Careful listening lets you understand what your classmates are saying so you can build on their ideas.

items.prompt:
A student interrupts her classmate in the middle of his sentence. Which rule is she breaking?
A) Always use complete sentences
B) Speak one at a time and listen to others
C) Only the teacher can ask questions
items.answer: B) Speak one at a time and listen to others

steps: Interrupting breaks two rules: it prevents the speaker from finishing (speak one at a time) and shows lack of care for what they are saying (listen to others).

items.prompt:
A student says: 'I agree with what you said.' Is this enough to fully build on a classmate's idea?
A) Yes — agreeing is always enough
B) No — it is good to agree, but you should also add a new connected idea or explain why you agree
C) No — you should never agree in a discussion
items.answer: B) No — it is good to agree, but you should also add a new connected idea or explain why you agree

steps: Agreeing is a good start, but building on ideas means adding new information, a reason, or a connected thought.

items.prompt:
What is the name for conversations where students work together to share ideas and learn from each other?
A) Competitive debates
B) Collaborative discussions
C) Silent reading

steps: Collaborative discussions are conversations where students cooperate — listening, building on ideas, and learning from each other.
